component_records.title: Bid qualification, teaming and proposal compliance
component_records.description: We bid as a non-profit or for-profit lead entity with a documented track record in AI or closely related workforce development, and we evidence experience in at least three of the four required domains (academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training, serving low-income populations, New York market work). Where we team, one organization is designated lead and holds contracting authority, and the proposal states that structure explicitly. The administrative volume is assembled in the RFP's listed order and includes the Non-Collusive Bidding Certification, Conflict of Interest Attestation, State Finance Law §§139-j/139-k forms, Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire completed within one year, Iran Divestment Act Statement, EO-16 and EO-177 certifications, OCSD-1/2/4 forms, NYS Businesses form, ST-220-CA or affidavit, and W-9, with a completeness check before upload. We also confirm financial ability, organizational capacity, legal authority, integrity of the firm and its principals, and satisfactory performance of prior government contracts, and we review the EO-192 vendor integrity requirements. The proposal is uploaded to the designated Dropbox as a main folder named per the convention with separate Administrative and Technical subfolders, and we accept the RFP's conditions by submitting.

component_records.title: Procurement integrity and restricted-period governance
component_records.description: A named bid and contract-compliance lead owns all contact with ESD, restricting communication to the designated contacts Julia Borukhov and Jordan Kaplan at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov for the whole restricted period through contract approval, and logging every exchange. The same lead files the State Finance Law §§139-j and 139-k disclosure and affirmation forms and keeps them current through the contract term, and confirms the firm's sole responsibility for full compliance with those Procurement Requirements. We operate a no-gifts and no-employment-offer rule covering ESD employees, members and directors, including the 30-day post-involvement window, and we disclose any existing or contemplated relationship with ESD staff, 5%+ shareholders, parents, subsidiaries or affiliates that could be an actual or apparent conflict. Questions are submitted in writing by the August 29, 2025 deadline; no oral questions are taken.

component_records.title: Program design, curriculum and training delivery
component_records.description: We deliver the AI Prep program itself for Track A and/or Track B: an industry-informed AI curriculum built with leading researchers and employer input, delivered as online AI courses with mentorship and real-world machine-learning projects, and refreshed each cohort against employer demand. Track A gives low-income matriculating undergraduates AI training aimed at paid internships at leading tech companies; Track B gives low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment an accelerated bootcamp alternative to a degree program. Training is immersive and available in part-time and full-time schedules, with stated duration, weekly hours, cohort size and academic-year or summer timing aligned to employer internship hiring cycles. We state the credentials awarded on completion, measure skill attainment through defined evaluation metrics during training, and provide professional development support throughout. The program creates a direct education-to-AI-industry pathway and builds a talent pipeline for AI employers.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment, application and needs assessment
component_records.description: We run a targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income New Yorkers, working through colleges and universities, community organizations and nonprofit partners, with a stated definition of low-income and a documented verification method. A structured application and evaluation process screens for eligibility and readiness, and every admitted participant receives a needs assessment that identifies barriers — income, childcare, transportation, device and connectivity access, academic preparation — and routes them to the support that removes them. We commit to a participant volume that clears the 250 minimum and targets the 400-plus priority band, with more than 50% of participants low-income, and we report applicant, enrollment and completion counts with low-income percentages.

component_records.title: Stipends, wraparound supports and coaching
component_records.description: Every participant receives a stated stipend level plus wraparound supports, budgeted explicitly as a line in the Wraparound Supports and Participant Stipend Level category. Supports include mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise, success coaching for Track B participants, and practical assistance such as devices, connectivity, transportation and childcare referrals identified in the needs assessment. Coaches carry caseloads sized to the cohort plan and stay with participants through training and into placement, which is how we hold completion and placement rates rather than just enrollment.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships, internships and job placement
component_records.description: An employer-relations team cultivates and maintains relationships with leading New York tech employers, both to inform curriculum content and to generate paid internship slots, and we attach employer partner letters committing to paid internships or full-time jobs. We help students secure paid internships where they apply their new AI skills to real-world work and build the networks that lead to full-time roles, and we provide full-time job connection support in AI or a closely related field for Track B graduates and Track A alumni. Placement is tracked as a rate, with the majority of graduates targeted into paid internships or full-time AI employment, and we coordinate directly with individual employers on matching, onboarding and performance feedback.

component_records.title: Performance data, reporting and quality assurance
component_records.description: We stand up a participant data system at mobilization that captures, at minimum, applicant counts and low-income percentage, enrollment counts and low-income percentage, completion counts and low-income percentage, paid internship placement rate and low-income share of placements, full-time job placement rate and low-income share, participating colleges and universities, and participating employer partners, and we make that data available to ESD on request in ESD's agreed format. We commit annual performance estimates against total participants served, low-income completion percentage and placement rate, justified from historical results and partner commitments, and we report against them. Services are performed to applicable professional standards, with any service that fails those standards and produces obvious or patent errors corrected at no charge, and we support ESD's performance assessment through progress reports and periodic meetings on an agreed schedule.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
component_records.description: We submit a line-by-line price proposal with Personnel Services broken out by job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percentage of time and cost to contract, and Other Than Personnel Services costs on separate lines with quantities and cost to contract. The budget is mapped to the 18-month program duration, includes staff salary and benefits and the wraparound and stipend level, and excludes indirect costs entirely. It stays within $2M for one track and $4M for both, and it states the extent of any voluntary cost match in ESD's budget template. Other program costs such as curriculum development, marketing and events are itemized and justified, and the whole budget is accompanied by a written justification tying each line to a deliverable.

component_records.title: Staffing, subcontracting and change control
component_records.description: We propose named key personnel with one-page resumes, and we accept that assigned staff are subject to ESD approval, that each proposed substitute comes with a summary of experience and an interview opportunity before approval, and that our people, agents, consultants and subcontractors are qualified in experience, knowledge and character for their duties. We commit to keeping staff on the project to completion and to notifying ESD immediately of any proposed staff change. The agreement is not assigned or transferred, and no service is subcontracted unless it is identified in our proposal or ESD's State Project Manager gives prior written approval; all employees of ours and our subcontractors hold the required qualifications, training, licenses and permits, are legally entitled to work where services are performed, and comply with federal and state employment law. We continue performing as modified while any change claim is pending, and we assert any price or time adjustment claim within 30 days of written notice of a Corporation-ordered change; added services stay within the contract's general scope and exclude licensed professional work such as engineering, architectural, environmental consulting, abatement, treatment or testing.

component_records.title: MWBE, SDVOB and workforce diversity compliance
component_records.description: We submit an MWBE Utilization Plan and an SDVOB Utilization Plan on Form OCSD-4 with the proposal, committing to the 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB participation goals, counting only sums paid for a commercially useful function and applying the 25% broker rule where a broker is used. We demonstrate good faith efforts through the New York State Contract System, including copies of solicitations to SDVOBs and responses, reasons each responding SDVOB was not selected, dates of ESD-scheduled meetings with certified SDVOBs, and the steps taken to structure scope for SDVOB subcontracting, and we consult the state SDVOB directory and MWBE directory when sourcing. We accept Schedule B in full, agree that ESD may withhold payment pending MWBE documentation, and accept that willful failure to meet the goals is a breach with liquidated damages equal to the shortfall against goal sums. We report quarterly MWBE Contractor Compliance and Payment, quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports including gross wages per Executive Order #162, and monthly SDVOB compliance on Form OCSD-6 by the 10th of each month to OCSD@esd.ny.gov, and we respond to any notice of deficiency within seven business days, filing an OCSD-5 waiver request within five business days if the remedy is rejected. We speak with the designated contacts before any waiver request, file post-award waiver requests no later than before final payment, and maintain non-discrimination and equal employment opportunity practices including Human Rights Law compliance and non-discrimination on prior conviction or arrest.

items.text: The RFP is issued by Empire State Development (ESD), a New York State economic development corporation whose mission is to promote a growing state economy, encourage business investment and job creation, and support diverse local economies through loans, grants, tax credits, real estate development and marketing.

ESD's Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) was created under Governor Hochul's April 2022 $350 million workforce development investment and is charged with aligning workforce programs to employer needs and creating opportunities for unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented workers in high-growth sectors, with AI named as one of those sectors.

ESD's stated pain point is that rapid AI advancement may widen economic inequality, because well-paying AI jobs require specialized education and technical training that low-income New Yorkers often cannot access, and tech recruiting favors elite-school students and those with personal connections to prominent technology companies.

New York State is positioned as an AI hub through institutions such as Cornell Tech and state-backed initiatives such as Empire AI, and ESD frames AI Prep as reinforcing that position while creating opportunity in the sector.

The procurement is subject to a Restricted Period under the Procurement Lobbying Law running until contract approval, during which respondents may contact only the designated contacts Julia Borukhov (primary) and Jordan Kaplan (secondary) at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.

ESD seeks to award contracts to up to two qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and administer AI Prep, an applied AI training program that connects low-income New Yorkers to AI internships and jobs.
